summary: Build report pages bespoke and with soft-ui, then judge each pair blind for intent match

a_only: Expenses this year as its own KPI ($565,493)
Revenue last year (Jan-Nov) as its own KPI card
Bank, savings, owed to us, and we owe shown as separate KPI cards
Folded month-by-month table with revenue, last year, growth, expenses, profit, and margin each month
b_only: A KPI for total overdue invoices ($33,140, with $7,120 over 60 days)
Profit-each-month bar chart that marks thin-margin months and shows the average
Net position line ($161,880) in a cash-position ledger
Overdue total row and a call-to-action note on who to chase
Percentage shares and amounts for each expense category and each customer
Data-quality footnotes (categories and customers do not add up to the monthly totals, no 2025 expenses, Kereru bucket)
The note that costs are rising almost as fast as revenue
judge.why: B puts revenue, last year, and expenses on one chart with profit shaded, and adds a profit-by-month view, so the owner sees the health and the cost trend at a glance. B also labels each bar with its amount and share, and flags the data gaps; A puts the per-month numbers in a folded table and charts "Others" as the largest customer bar.

fixed_lines: fixed layout[2].section[1].table: dropped unknown prop "collapse". Next time: use only known props (table props: data, cols, sort, group, filter, search, limit, bar, tone, fmt, expand, top, order, labels, good, dense)
tool.friction: (1) The callout cannot reference computed values. A headline such as "revenue $662k, up 12.6%, profit $96.7k, cash = 2.4 months of expenses, $33.1k overdue" had to be computed outside the tool with a Python one-liner and typed in by hand. That conflicts with the rule "do not type numbers that the data holds". Chart notes such as "10 of 11 months" and "77% of expenses" have the same problem. A template form like {{sum monthly.revenue | money}} in callout and note would fix it. (2) The stat `vs` subline prints the raw column name ("vs $587,954 revenue_last_year"). I found no prop to label it. (3) The stats `cols` tiles use column names as labels, so I had to add a `rename` step on the dataset to get "Owed to us". A `labels` map on stats would be simpler. (4) Only a card can collapse. I first put `collapse` on a table, which was auto-fixed (dropped), and then wrapped the table in a card. (5) The data does not reconcile, and the page does not say so: expenses_by_category sums to $496.5k but the monthly expenses sum to $565.5k, and top_customers sums to $631.9k against $662.2k of revenue. A reconciliation or check step would help. (6) I wanted things I could not easily show: a derived cash-runway stat (cash / mean monthly expenses) computed from two datasets, a profit-margin line on the revenue/expense chart (a second axis or combo bar+line), and a mark on the ageing chart at the 60-day overdue boundary for a category axis. I also could not give stat tiles a sparkline from a data column (`spark` takes only a typed list). (7) Sorting by `days_overdue` puts the oldest debts first, which was right. My first title, "latest first", described that order wrongly; I fixed it to "most late first", which still reads awkwardly.
